articles.headline: NFL Week 8: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 8.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第8週：日曜の試合から見る重要事項、疑問点、ファンタジー視点の分析
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationのレポーター陣がすべての試合展開に反応し、日曜日の各試合から生じた最大の疑問に答えます。第8週のまとめをお届けします。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off with some shocking results in the early window, including two overtime finishes.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb on his first snap back after missing three games with an ankle injury, allowing the Bills to cruise to an easy win. The Vikings lost their first game of the season, scoring just 15 points against a Lions defense that had allowed 20-plus points five times in 2026. And despite not completing a pass, the Buccaneers shut out the Falcons.

In the late window Sunday, the Chargers lost in an L.A. showdown versus the Rams. It marked the third time that quarterback Justin Herbert threw multiple interceptions (two) this season.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

LAC-LAR | TEN-CIN | ARI-DAL

BAL-BUF | LV-NYJ | MIN-DET

CLE-PIT | IND-JAX | ATL-TB

Catch up on Thursday's game:

CAR-GB

New England 24, Miami 19

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Patriots

Can Patriots sustain playing this way? The first half was their worst of the season (just 98 yards on offense), and while they exploded in the second half, they might not be as fortunate in the next two weeks against better competition -- home against the Packers and then against the Lions in Munich, Germany. The big play bailed them out, with quarterback Drake Maye -- who was excellent while facing heavy pressure -- throwing touchdown passes to Kyle Williams (43 yards) and DeMario Douglas (48-yard catch-and-run). It was the Patriots' first game with multiple receiving TDs of 40-plus yards since Sept. 24, 2017, versus the Texans.

Trend to watch: Injuries impacting the Patriots' roster. Starting tight end Hunter Henry (foot) left the game in the first half and didn't return, while promising rookie outside linebacker Gabe Jacas (knee) left the game in the third quarter and did not return. The team already entered the game without starting wide receiver A.J. Brown (knee) and No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness). -- Mike Reiss

Next game: vs. Packers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Dolphins

For a team still learning how to win, what lesson can the Dolphins take away from today's game? Mainly that games are not over until they're over, which is a lesson this young Dolphins team got an introduction to in last week's win over the Jets. Miami held a two-score lead at halftime for the second consecutive week, and its offense sputtered in the third quarter for the second consecutive week. This time, the Patriots came back to re-take the lead -- something good teams do. Oct. 30: Packers' ground game cause for concern

By Adam Rank

Jordan Love throws multiple touchdown passes. Matthew Golden looks good. I mean, Christian Watson left and arrived back at Lambeau Field from an ambulance in a move that would make Triple H say, "no way this is real." And yet, I get a note from my editor (a Packers fan, mind you) complaining about the (lack of a) Green Bay Packers running game. 

I mean, the Milwaukee Brewers just won the World Series, but we need to focus on the Packers' rushing attack? Well, I guess that is the best place to start.

The Packers won the game despite rushing for just 66 yards. They have been held to fewer than 90 rushing yards in all eight games, the club's longest streak in the Super Bowl era. The Packers' 485 rushing yards are the fewest by any team through eight games since the 2019 Bengals. I mean, what in the name of Eddie Lee Ivery is going on here?

The short answer is the offensive line is bad. The playcalling is bad. I mean, you think the guy who favored Dion Lewis over Derrick Henry when he was offensive coordinator in Tennessee was ever going to have a solid running game in Green Bay? It's just the facts.

And it's not going to get much easier in the coming weeks, either. The New England Patriots, Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Rams aren't great matchups. It's not until the New Orleans Saints in Week 13 that the schedule softens for Josh Jacobs. If you kept him on your roster all this time, you're likely going to be compelled to start him, but the matchups aren't ideal.

Some other notes from Thursday night:

Love has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all eight games this season, but this was his first game of the season with three touchdown passes. He's a set-and-forget quarterback moving forward. It is wild to think he wasn't drafted as a QB1 this year.

Watson is nearing ace territory this season. He recorded his 12th reception of 20-plus yards, second in the league behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

articles.headline: Maye has 3 touchdowns as Patriots rally to beat Dolphins 24-19
articles.description: — Drake Maye threw two touchdown passes and rushed for a score as the New England Patriots came back to beat the Miami Dolphins 24-19 on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: メイが3タッチダウン、ペイトリオッツが猛追しドルフィンズに24-19で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ドレイク・メイが2つのパスによるタッチダウンとランによるタッチダウンを決め、ニューイングランド・ペイトリオッツは日曜日の試合でマイアミ・ドルフィンズに24-19で逆転勝利を収めた。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- — Drake Maye threw two touchdown passes and rushed for a score as the New England Patriots came back to beat the Miami Dolphins 24-19 on Sunday.


              With star receiver AJ Brown inactive because of lingering injuries, Maye completed 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards and the Patriots (5-3) rallied from a 10-point halftime deficit to take a 17-13 lead entering the fourth, then held on after a late Miami rally.


              DeMario Douglas caught a pass and weaved through the Dolphins secondary for a 48-yard touchdown catch that put the Patriots up two scores early in the fourth.


              The Patriots hadn’t had a clean operation in the first half, but they took advantage of the young Dolphins’ mistakes in the second, outscoring Miami 21-0 until Malik Willis threw a 35-yard touchdown to rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. with two minutes left. 


              After an unsuccessful two-point try by Miami, Stevenson recovered Bradley Pinion's onside kick, and New England kept the ball from there.


              Stevenson had 19 carries for 82 yards, and Douglas caught three passes for 76 yards.


              One week after leading Miami (1-6) to its first win of the season, Willis completed 21 of 32 passes for 211 yards. He threw for two touchdowns and had an interception while being sacked five times. 


              The Patriots pulled within three when Maye lofted a pass to Kyle Williams for a 43-yard touchdown that was initially ruled an incompletion after Williams' knee appeared to jar the ball loose. When coach Mike Vrabel demonstratively launched the red challenge flag, officials overturned the call to a touchdown after replays showed Williams crossed the goal line before losing possession of the ball. 


              Miami went three-and-out on the next drive, its momentum stalled after Ollie Gordon drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty after saying something to a defender following a 5-yard carry. Coach Jeff Hafley removed Gordon from the game for a play, and the second-year running back appeared visibly upset on the sideline.


              Maye faked a pitch to Rhamondre Stevenson and ran it in for the 2-yard go-ahead score with 59 seconds left in the third — his fifth straight game with at least three total touchdowns.


              Willis led the Dolphins on an 11-play, 70-yard two-minute drive that Malik Washington capped a 1-yard touchdown to put Miami ahead 13-3 at the half. 


              Washington had briefly left the game after taking a hard hit from Patriots linebacker Christian Elliss earlier in the drive. Elliss was flagged for unnecessary roughness for the hit, and Washington, after a brief trip to the blue medial tent, returned five plays later to catch his first receiving touchdown of the season.

articles.headline: Cardinals' LaFleur noncommittal on QB after Minshew replaces Brissett in win
articles.description: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur wouldn't commit to next week's starting quarterback after Gardner Minshew replaced Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter Sunday and led Arizona to a comeback win over Dallas.
articles.headlineJa: カージナルスのラフルア監督、ミンシューがブリスレットに代わり勝利を収めるも、次週のQBについては明言を避ける
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日の第3クォーター、ガードナー・ミンシューがジャコビー・ブリスレットに代わって出場し、アリゾナをダラスに対する逆転勝利へと導いたことを受け、カージナルスのマイク・ラフルア監督は来週の先発クォーターバックについて明言を避けた。
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Arizona Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur wouldn't commit to next week's starting quarterback after he replaced starter Jacoby Brissett with Gardner Minshew with 95 seconds left in the third quarter of Sunday's 33-30 overtime win against the Dallas Cowboys. 

"I'm just excited about this win right now," LaFleur said when asked if Minshew will start Sunday at Seattle. 

However, a source told ESPN the expectation is that Minshew will continue as Arizona's quarterback.

LaFleur said he made the switch to Minshew to spark Arizona's offense, which, until the move, trailed 17-3 and saw its red zone woes continue. Arizona failed to score a touchdown in its first two trips to the red zone Sunday, extending its run to 1-for-12.

The Cardinals ended their red zone drought when Minshew took over, scoring three times inside the 20-yard-line. 

LaFleur said the decision to change quarterbacks didn't hinge on one person.

"It was a collective deal," LaFleur said. "I need to be better with our scheme, obviously. I need to be better with our playcalling and all of us need it. We got a lot to fix right now and I don't want this last 30 minutes or 35 minutes to mask the stuff that we need to fix on offense because I know we're a lot better than that. I know we can execute better than that."

While he waits to hear if he'll start next week, Minshew said he plans to take every day one at a time and will come to work Monday "and give it our best, regardless."

"So, doesn't change much," he said.

Except Minshew changed Arizona's record Sunday.

He brought Arizona back from a two-touchdown deficit to tie the score at 30 with six seconds left on a 13-yard touchdown pass to Michael Wilson, who was playing with two broken ribs. But kicker Chad Ryland missed the extra point, which sent the game into overtime. 

Ryland was able to avenge his miss with a 42-yard game-winning field goal to give Arizona its third win of the season. 

"He did a good job," LaFleur said of Minshew. "Obviously extended a few plays, stuff like that, but I thought his timing was great. I mean he's had a lot of success in this league and he's about as resilient as they come, too. If you ask Gardner Minshew, he's ready at all times. I thought the guys made some plays for him and he was getting the ball out of his hands."

Minshew executed the Cardinals' comeback without a slew of regular players.

Jeremiyah Love left in the first half with his third ankle injury of the season and did not return. Then wide receiver Kendrick Bourne suffered an ankle injury that left him on crutches and "certainly didn't look good," according to LaFleur. Running back Bam Knight suffered a concussion and did not return, leaving the Cardinals with just Tyler Allgeier as their lone active running back.

articles.headline: Jayson Tatum's 32, Paul George's 10 4th-quarter points lead Boston Celtics to win at Orlando
articles.description: — Jayson Tatum scored 32 points — 15 of them from the free-throw line — and Paul George added 17 as the Boston Celtics won their fifth straight, 108-97 over the Orlando Magic Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイソン・テイタムの32得点、ポール・ジョージの第4Qでの10得点がボストン・セルティックスをオーランドでの勝利へ導く
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイソン・テイタムが32得点（うち15得点はフリースロー）を挙げ、ポール・ジョージが17得点を加えたボストン・セルティックスは、日曜日にオーランド・マジックを108-97で破り、5連勝を飾った。
articles.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. -- — Jayson Tatum scored 32 points — 15 of them from the free-throw line — and Paul George added 17 as the Boston Celtics won their fifth straight, 108-97 over the Orlando Magic Sunday.


              Anthony Black and Tristan da Silva each scored 23 to lead the Magic (2-4), who dropped to 0-3 at home. Orlando forward Franz Wagner had 14 points and a career-high 12 assists.


              Boston (5-1) also got a pair of critical blocks from Neemias Queta in the final two minutes, and George’s 3-pointer with 1:32 remaining gave Boston an insurmountable 11-point lead.


              The Celtics built a 15-point lead by shutting out Orlando over the first four minutes of the second half. Orlando battled back on the strength of three of da Silva’s five 3-pointers, using a 12-0 run to cut Boston’s lead to 77-74 entering the final period.


              And early in the fourth quarter, Black completed a three-point play to tie it at 79, picking the pocket of George on an outlet pass. But on the following possession, Wagner couldn’t sink a layup to give Orlando the lead.


              With Paolo Banchero (high-ankle sprain) missing his fourth straight game, Boston constantly keyed on Wagner.


              But every time Orlando got close, Tatum slammed the door. Boston’s perennial All-Star made 15 of his 17 attempts from the free-throw line. Orlando as a team had just 19 free-throw attempts.


              Tatum left late in the first quarter after the back of his head collided inadvertently with the forehead of Orlando’s Jamal Cain. Bleeding, Tatum visited the locker room but returned with 6:13 left in the first half.


              Queta started in place of center Mitchell Robinson, who missed the game due to rest. Luka Garza (12 points) and Baylor Scheierman (10) were in double figures for Boston, which leads the NBA in bench scoring.


              Up next
              Celtics: At Houston on Monday night.


              Magic: Host Washington on Monday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Kerim Alajbegovic and Jérémie Boga hit stunners as Juventus beat 10-man Napoli
articles.description: Kerim Alajbegovic and Jérémie Boga scored stunning second-half goals as Juventus beat 10-man Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium to ease the pressure on head coach Luciano Spalletti.
articles.headlineJa: ケリム・アライベゴビッチとジェレミー・ボガが鮮烈なゴール、ユヴェントスが10人となったナポリを下す
articles.descriptionJa: アリアンツ・スタジアムで行われた試合で、ケリム・アライベゴビッチとジェレミー・ボガが後半に素晴らしいゴールを決め、ユヴェントスが10人となったナポリを2-0で破ってルチアーノ・スパレッティ監督へのプレッシャーを軽減した。
articles.body:
Kerim Alajbegovic and Jérémie Boga scored stunning second-half goals as Juventus beat 10-man Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium to ease the pressure on head coach Luciano Spalletti.

Juve, who had won only one of their four previous Serie A matches, had been jeered by their own fans earlier in the second period before Bosnian teenager Alajbegovic and Boga both struck with long-range efforts.

Napoli, who slipped to their fourth league defeat of the season, had defender Luca Marianucci sent off soon after Juve's opener for his second yellow card.

Napoli went close to taking an early lead as Lorenzo Lucca's early diving header was brilliantly saved by Juve goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario.

Juve's first chance was blazed over the crossbar by Jhon Lucumí in the 16th minute and they went closer soon after when Colombia defender Juan Cabal's close-range effort hit a post.

Both sides continued to create chances before the break, but lacked quality in front of goal.

Scoring chances at both ends dried up after the restart and there were whistles and jeers from the home fans after Randal Kolo Muani's misplaced pass.

Juve skipper Bremer headed Douglas Luiz's cross straight at Alex Meret before Alajbegovic's first Serie A goal gave Juve supporters something to cheer as he slammed a 20-yard shot into the top corner.

Napoli were dealt a further blow five minutes later when centre-half Marianucci received his second yellow card for his rash challenge on Cabal.

And it got worse for the visitors when Boga, an earlier replacement for Alajbegovic, cut in from the left and curled a superb finish into the far corner.

articles.headline: Arteta says Arsenal 'loved the mission' in first Anfield win since 2012
articles.description: Mikel Arteta said his players "loved the mission" of winning at Liverpool for the first time in 14 years as he hailed Sunday's "historic" 1-0 victory at Anfield.
articles.headlineJa: アルテタ監督、2012年以来初のアニフィールド勝利に「ミッションを楽しんでいた」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタ監督は、日曜日のアニフィールドでの「歴史的」な1-0の勝利を称賛し、選手たちが14年ぶりとなるリヴァプールでの勝利という「ミッションを楽しんでいた」と語った。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta said his players "loved the mission" of winning at Liverpool for the first time in 14 years as he hailed Sunday's "historic" 1-0 victory at Anfield.

Kai Havertz's 16th-minute strike was enough to secure a narrow win in a hard-fought game that sent the Gunners three points clear at the top of the Premier League ahead of Manchester City.

Liverpool put Arsenal under huge pressure after falling behind, but the visitors kept them at bay with a more controlled second-half display, and the Reds ended without registering a shot on target for the first time ever in a Premier League home game.

Arsenal had lost eight of their past 13 league games and kept just one clean sheet in 27 previous league visits to Anfield before Sunday.

"[They are] just loving the mission," said Arteta. "And the mission was something that we didn't accomplish in 14 years. There were reasons for that. Some of them were psychological problems. Some of them were related to the quality that we showed on the pitch, certain moments or decisions.

"And we knew that we need to nail absolutely all of them. And we're going to have to navigate through periods that we're going to have to suffer because they are extremely good at doing that and creating those vertical attacks, those chaos moments for almost nothing.

"You really need to enjoy that. If you don't, there will be a moment they will switch up and they will punish you. And yeah, I think the way we competed and played and the chances that we generated as well, it was really impressive. So I'm really happy."

Arsenal, after being dumped out of the Carabao Cup by League Two side Fleetwood Town in midweek, responded with a defiant display to extend their record in the Premier League to eight wins and one loss from nine games.

"We're extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody's done especially in the conditions that we arrived to this game, where we were after the defeat against Liverpool, it looks like the end of the world," Arteta said. "It looks like, 'Yeah, what are we doing?' And then you have to pick yourself up and understand that this is a beautiful part of this game.

"It can take you to really bad places, but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic, and we've done it."

articles.headline: Arsenal hold on for a big win at Liverpool, one Iraola & Co. can learn from
articles.description: Arsenal's defense held firm against the Reds' expensive attack to notch a famous win at Anfield for the first time since 2012. However, there were positive signs for Liverpool when it came to their intensity and effort.
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL -- Arsenal made a huge statement in the Premier League title race by securing a 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

 
A first-half goal from Kai Havertz was enough to seal the Gunners' first win at Liverpool's home stadium in over 14 years. The result sees Mikel Arteta's move to the top of the Premier League table, three points clear of second-placed Manchester City.

 
Havertz opened the scoring inside 17 minutes, tapping in at the far post from Declan Rice's cross. However, Liverpool responded well to the early setback and were frustrated not to have been awarded a penalty for Jurriën Timber's shirt pull on Alexander Isak inside the box.

 
The Reds came close to restoring parity late in the first half when Alexis Mac Allister nodded over the bar after a dangerous ball into the box from Milos Kerkez. Arsenal later had a big chance to double their lead when Christos Tzolis saw his low drive tipped around the post by Alisson. Ultimately though, Havertz's goal was enough to secure all three points for Arteta's side and to end Liverpool's five-game winning run in all competitions. -- Beth Lindop

1. Arsenal end their Anfield hoodoo with gritty defensive display

Arsenal just don't win at Anfield. They have not recorded a victory on this ground since Sept. 2012 -- when manager Mikel Arteta was a player. Often they have crumbled here -- think 4-0 in 2021, 5-1 in 2018 or 4-0 in 2017 -- and even last season when there were already early signs that Liverpool looked vulnerable in their title defence, Arsenal were too passive and lost to a brilliant 83rd-minute Dominik Szoboszlai free-kick.

- VAR Review: Were Liverpool denied a clear penalty?

And so they arrived at this famous old ground with familiar questions around their character, especially after losing to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup, and how they would go about it: go to dominate like they attempted at Bayern Munich, or slip into a more familiar conservative approach?

Their bravery was ultimately rewarded.

Arsenal dug in for long periods, particularly in the first half, but that was simply due to the quality of Liverpool's response to falling behind. They restricted Liverpool to little of note in the second half, aided by a bold substitution as Arteta replaced Bruno Guimarães with the more attack-minded Myles Lewis-Skelly on 62 minutes.

It is fitting that Arsenal went top of the table with a statement win like this. There is now only Premier League ground left in which Arteta has played and never won: Manchester City. -- James Olley

2. Liverpool need to learn from Arsenal's defending

The game was only 20 minutes old when Bruno Guimares celebrated a block inside his own penalty area with the same enthusiasm as if he'd scored a goal. It was an embodiment of Arsenal's unerring commitment to defending, something Liverpool need to learn from if they have ambitions of challenging for major honours in the near future.

articles.headline: Ex-Liverpool, Man City star Milner runs NYC Marathon in just over three hours
articles.description: It's clear James Milner is enjoying his retirement from soccer, as he ran the 2026 NYC Marathon on Sunday with an impressive time. Did we mention he's 40 years old?
articles.body:
James Milner has always been something of a cult hero in soccer, with his work ethic and personable demeanor making him a fan favorite across a 24-year career, especially at the clubs he represented. From Leeds United to Newcastle United, Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool and Brighton, Milner made a career for being the hardest working, indefatigable presence in every team, routinely finishing tops of preseason fitness tests even as he celebrated turning 40 back in January.

He announced his retirement at the end of the 2025-26 season but do you think for one minute that "Milly" has taken it easier now that he's hung up his boots?

Of course he hasn't: On Sunday, he seemingly cruised his way through the 2026 New York City Marathon, completing the course in a remarkable 3:09.04. Not bad, James, not bad at all!

Looking deeper at his split times, it does seem as though Milner took it easy (well, easier) down the stretch, wrapping the first half in 1:31 before going 1:38 for the final 13 miles, but we forgive him for turning it into more of a fun run from there. That said, an average pace of 7:13 per mile is remarkable; it makes us tired just reading it.

What's next, Milner: climbing Mount Everest? Playing in the NFL? We wouldn't bet against him regardless of what he sets his sights on ...

articles.headline: Jalen Brunson joins Harry Styles on stage to cap Styles' MSG residency
articles.description: The superstar singer-songwriter was joined on stage by Brunson, who presented Styles with a commemorative banner for his 30-show Madison Square Garden residency.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ブランソンがハリー・スタイルズのステージに登場、MSGレジデンシーの締めくくりに
articles.descriptionJa: 超人気シンガーソングライターのステージにブランソンが共演。マディソン・スクエア・ガーデンでの30公演にわたるレジデンシーを記念して、スタイルズに記念バナーを贈呈した。
articles.body:
Harry Styles brings plenty of fame to the stage as-is, but the superstar singer-songwriter's Saturday night performance at Madison Square Garden got an extra boost in star power from a guest plenty familiar with the Garden's spotlight.

Star New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson.

Saturday night marked the 30th show of Styles' Together, Together residency, and he was joined on stage by Brunson, who presented Styles with a commemorative banner for the residency. Brunson, who was received with uproarious "MVP" chants from the home crowd, rocked a hat emblazoned with "TECHNO IS MY BOYFRIEND," which Styles has been known to don himself.

"Can you just make a note, we're almost as tall as each other," Styles joked when the two greeted each other on stage.

"And, yes, I will return your hat," Brunson responded.

It's not the first time during Styles' residency that Brunson has made an appearance. The newly minted NBA champion had already attended two of Styles' previous shows during his stretch of performances at the Garden, getting a shoutout from the singer on Sept. 12.

"We may or may not have the King of New York in the house tonight ... Mr. Jalen Brunson," Styles said during the show. "He's just trying to have a quiet night out -- not a chance. Not in this city. It's like Mickey Mouse going to Disneyland."

Brunson will return to his own Madison Square Garden stage Monday when the Knicks host the Brooklyn Nets.

What you need to know for Sunday

November opens with a quartet of NBA games, each of which could prove to be competitive according to betting metrics, as today's point spreads range from just 2.5-6.5 points.

Tighter lines suggest the potential for close games, a welcome environment for fantasy purposes given the greater predictability of playing time and workloads when games are tight and coaching patterns remain steadier.

The absence of Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac for the Pacers spells another big role for combo guard Andrew Nembhard. Third-year forward Jarace Walker could help in deeper leagues thanks to his ability to do a little bit of everything.

articles.body:
Sacramento Kings (0-6, 15th in the Western Conference) vs. Dallas Mavericks (4-2, seventh in the Western Conference)


              Dallas; Monday, 8 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Dallas will look to keep its three-game win streak intact when the Mavericks take on Sacramento.


              Dallas went 26-56 overall and 14-37 in Western Conference play a season ago. The Mavericks averaged 114.1 points per game while shooting 46.6% from the field and 34.4% from 3-point distance last season.


              Sacramento went 22-60 overall and 14-38 in Western Conference games during the 2025-26 season. The Kings shot 46.7% from the field and 34.0% from 3-point range last season.


              INJURIES: Mavericks: Santi Aldama: day to day (knee), Tarik Biberovic: day to day (heel), Sergio De Larrea: out (knee), Dereck Lively II: day to day (foot).


              Kings: Ben Simmons: out for season (achilles), Keegan Murray: out (ankle), Dylan Cardwell: out (calf), Maxime Raynaud: out (knee).
